### 2026-10-14 – So I started my project yesterday, even though I'm logging the Journal today(soon I will start using time-lapses once I figure it out).

**2.6h**

So I started my project yesterday, even though I'm logging the Journal today(soon I will start using time-lapses once I figure it out).

Anyways, for the first 30 minutes, I did some research about the following three things:

  --- 1. Do I want to add electronics, or make the 3D design work based on mechanical gears

--- 2. What CAD software do I want to use?

---3. What 3D print could be useful for me

Here's how I answered each one:

1. I decided not to use electronics since it would become too complicated. Also, I decided to use Onshape and made a mechanical lock box.

Next, I decided to learn Onshape (how it worked and what commands to use). I followed along and built a small cube box with a mechanical gear for the tutorial(took me around 1 hr.

Next, I spent 30 minutes working on my actual project. I started by making the box using extrusion/sketch(I got sooo stuck). Finally, I emptied the inside.

### 2026-10-18 – Hour 1:

**4h**

Hour 1:

I started by opening my CAD design in Onshape and looking at the main box that I had been working on. I wanted to make sure that the box had enough space for the moving door and the hinge. I looked at the different parts of the design and checked how they were positioned. I also used different views in Onshape to get a better understanding of how everything would fit together. One of the main things I focused on was figuring out where the hinge should be placed so the door could open and close without getting stuck.  It took me soooo long, but i figured it out.

Hour 2 — Designing the Hinge

After working on the main box, I focused on the hinge that would connect the door to the box. I worked with the circular parts of the hinge and checked their sizes and positions. I wanted to make sure that the hinge would allow the door to rotate properly.

![recatngela](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/OV6IDpCKgzeGxU5I6u0lX5O426KLPYWz/aeb25c6d4fa1445bc9d7febf2d71f125c354412999e8ff5103a54e03ad107d18.png)

Ok, so continuing on with the other two hinges, it took me 2 hours.....(ik it feels like a lot, but it's my first time using Onshape.....)

 I looked at how the gray hinge part connected to the dark blue door. This took some time because I needed to understand which parts would move and how they would stay connected. I checked the measurements of the smaller circular sections and worked on understanding how the hinge would fit into the design. The thing is, I was really confused about how hinges worked... and well, it made me sooo frustrated since it was confusing to think about visually.

Ok so this  is the breakdown of what i did, plus errors(sooo many erros):

Breakdown:

I created sketches of rectangles and circles for hinges and connected them to the door.
Then I extruded them(basically 3D versions of 2d ), making it easier to make the axle inside the hinges.

Errors:

I faced many errors, like the hinges not connecting; sometimes the sketches kept getting detailed because I didn't check them. I kept doing undo a nd restarting my sketches because I got the wrong measurements. In order to get measurements, I did the sketch, then pressed to change measurements. But for the second and third hinge, I found a hack: just type in a number after making the shape (lol, I can't even believe that I missed that tool!)

Anyways, I'm soooo close; can't wait to finish. Btw: I kinda changed the project into a safe that opens and closes. For week 7, I will add a small 3d pritn desing code mechanism, but for now, due to time restrictions and a family emergency trip, I can only do this much. In week seven, I will customise it more.

### 2026-10-18 – October 18- Nighttime

**5.5h**

October 18- Nighttime

Finished CAD model (made door and dial!!!)

I started by working on the door for my CAD model. I wanted the door to fit properly with the main box while still being able to open and close. To do that, I properly used the D command to check the distance from one point of the box to the next. Then I was able to create a new sketch for making a corner rectangle. Then I extruded the sketch and used fillet to make a round door.

![nah](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/OV6IDpCKgzeGxU5I6u0lX5O426KLPYWz/d0dd95e28ec9dd5c837ce7b8d186f3a6fe492b63bfce13c3f5cb3bacd18334f1.png)

After making the door, I used rectangles and circles in a new sketch to connect the door to the hinges. This allowed the door to connect to the hinges.

The third hour was spent on creating a dial. I made a new sketch with a circle and added a small extrude rectangle in the circle.I then added the lock part on the back of the door so that when turned, it allowed the door to unlock.  (took me 2 hours)
